links.outcome: Accuracy of citations in LLM outputs (accurate, misrepresented, fabricated) on spine surgery questions
links.effect: Gemini average score 0.97 with 26.2% fabrications; ChatGPT fabrication rose from 2.1% to 20.0% on patient questions; Copilot 55.1% score-1 citations and 31.6% non-peer-reviewed websites; OpenEvidence perfect accuracy.
links.quote: General purpose LLMs exhibit substantial and variable citation errors when queried on spine surgery topics.

links.outcome: Citation accuracy of retrieval-grounded OpenEvidence versus general-purpose LLMs
links.effect: OpenEvidence, indexing PubMed directly, achieved perfect accuracy; general purpose LLMs had substantial fabrications (e.g., Gemini 26.2%).
links.quote: OpenEvidence, which directly indexes PubMed and requires user verification as a healthcare professional, achieved perfect accuracy.

links.outcome: LLM citation accuracy for patient-level versus clinician-level prompts
links.effect: All general purpose LLMs performed worse on patient-level queries; ChatGPT score fell from 1.83 to 1.08 and fabrication rate rose from 2.1% to 20.0%.
links.quote: All general purpose LLMs performed worse on patient-level queries.

screen.reason: Evaluates citation accuracy and hallucination rates across 5 LLMs using simulated clinician vs patient persona prompts, but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or intervention practice.
